title: Streaming handshake and chunk semantics to ensure tool-call atomicity and reconnect determinism
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: The current event-stream implementation handles chunked JSONL tokens but lacks a deterministic handshake and chunk-level semantics for tool/function-call boundaries. This causes end-user clients to see duplicated or truncated function-call events after intermittent reconnects and complicates compatibility with third-party SDKs.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight streaming handshake and chunk semantics that: 1) makes function/tool-call boundaries atomic at the chunk level, 2) allows clients to detect and resume from the last fully-committed chunk without replaying incomplete tool-calls, and 3) is backward-compatible with existing JSONL/legacy SSE clients via an opt-in capability negotiation.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Server emits a concise initial handshake frame with stream epoch, sequence base, and an optional checkpoint token.
- Each chunk has a stable chunk-id and a small per-chunk status field (partial|committed|retracted).
- Tool/function-call frames are anchored to chunk-ids; a chunk marked committed implies all tool-calls inside are durable and safe to deliver on reconnect.
- Clients can request resume from chunk N and the server will not re-emit committed chunks unless a forced rewind flag is set by the user.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy clients receive identical JSONL tokens and can ignore handshake metadata; modern SDKs can negotiate capability flags at connection time.
- Integration tests that simulate flaky networks show no duplicated tool-call deliveries in 500 simulated reconnect scenarios.

Deliverables: 
- Protocol document (Confluence) describing handshake envelope, chunk-id generation, and resume rules.
- Runtime implementation: controller-level handshake emitter + chunk metadata in the event pipeline.
- SDK changes (node/python) to support negotiated resume and checkpointing.
- E2E test harness and load test scenarios (k6) validating behavior under jitter and partition events.

Non-goals: full snapshotting of model internal state or long-term persistence of every chunk beyond short-lived resume windows.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Initial design sync: agreed to avoid large binary tokens in handshake to keep SSE friendly. Key trade-off: including checkpoint token increases resume precision but binds us to server-side checkpoint lifecycle. Decision: checkpoint token optional; prefer chunk-id + committed flag as core resume primitive. - Maya

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4216. Prototype emits "x-rw-handshake" as a first SSE event and appends "chunk_id" and "status" fields to each JSON chunk. Early feedback from SDK team: prefer camelCase keys for JS SDK friendliness. - Ravi

2026-03-05 - Design review notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STRM/Chunk+Semantics+and+Handshake. Action items: (1) define chunk-id namespace (opaque UUIDv4 vs incrementing per-session). Decided on monotonic per-connection sequence with optional opaque epoch prefix to allow multi-backend routing. - Design/Platform

2026-03-08 - Load test run: used k6 scenario with 200 concurrent resumers and random 500ms-3s disconnects. Observed reduced duplicated tool-call rate from 6.2% -> 0.3% after commit flag implemented but saw 1.1% of clients fail to apply resume due to older proxies stripping initial SSE comment lines. Follow-up: add fallback header X-RW-Stream-Capabilities to HTTP handshake for proxies. - QA

2026-03-11 - Security review prep: content supervised. KMS-based checkpoint tokens considered but flagged for later cycle. For this release we mark security_review_required=true and restrict checkpoint token lifetime to 5 minutes. - Security

2026-03-12 - SDK alignment: Node SDK implemented negotiating capability header 'x-rw-client-capabilities: resume-v1'. Python SDK to follow. Need a short migration guide for external SDKs. - SDK Lead (Clara)

2026-03-14 - Engineering update: RFC merged to main: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/8f7b2c1. Working on runtime integration tests next. Blocker: some edge proxies (company-cdn) drop SSE initial comment preamble; ops investigating configuration change to preserve first-rate event. - Ravi
